rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest candidates all land inside carve-outs: chunk 2 "Push back where the summary misreads", line 26 "Read Claude's summary. Push back where it misreads." — "Claude's summary" is the artifact the student's own session just produced (session-artifact carve-out, line 25 compendium). Chunk 3 "Keep or revert the .gitignore edit", line 31 "the compound step added it to your .gitignore" — "it" = CLAUDE.local.md, named repeatedly in chunks 0-1 (sequential deck read, in-file reuse permitted). No pronoun/demonstrative anywhere in the body fails to resolve against same-file prior chunks or the session-artifact carve-out.
No sentence in the body (lines 1-49) points at another file by position. `close-the-ticket` is named only in the post-maintainer-cut Arc block (line 110), outside judged scope. No candidate to flag.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every backward reference points at a beat that exists.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Chunk 0, line 11: "The PR shipped and the ticket is closed." Arc block (line 110) confirms this exercise picks up from `close-the-ticket`, which does ship a PR and close a ticket per `getting-going.md` line 121's module flow (Ex2 fix-tests-first ships the PR, Ex3 close-the-ticket closes the ticket). Referenced beat exists.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No guess-before-reveal instruction anywhere in the body; this exercise is a compound/retro loop, not a live-demo beat.

Smallest chunk is chunk 3 (lines 29-32), 4 lines: "If `CLAUDE.local.md` wasn't already ignored, the compound step added it to your `.gitignore`. That is an uncommitted change now; commit it, or drop it." Self-carrying claim (an instruction plus a decision), not a wait-state bullet. No chunk in the file is content-free.

Each header's content matches: chunk 1 "Write your rules file from the session" → body writes the rules file (lines 15-21); chunk 2 "Push back where the summary misreads" → body pushes back (lines 26-27); chunk 3 "Keep or revert the .gitignore edit" → body does exactly that (line 31); chunk 4 "Sweep the session into your rules file one more time" → second sweep prompt (lines 35-40); chunk 5 "What you built" → recap (lines 46-48). No header the chunk's own content contradicts.

Checked all sub-items against the body: no 'Not X. Not Y. Z.' construction anywhere; no anaphora/epistrophe triples; no self-grading superlative (closest is line 9 "every push-back is a hint toward your own rules" — a claim about the student's own action, not a value-prop rating of the exercise, so it doesn't trip §13's leak); no number-plus-retraction pattern (body contains no bare percentages/counts of this shape); no abstraction-noun stacks (vocabulary stays concrete: PR, ticket, rules file, .gitignore, scrollback); no empty-leg verb triplets. None of the six sub-items fire in any chunk.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Internal dialect never lands on a slide.
rules_evaluated.evidence: grep for repo dialect terms (surface-as-noun, firing, compendium, forcing function, beat, mood, Connections) in the body (lines 1-49): no hits. "compound engineering" (line 11) is the exercise's actual external subject matter (Klaassen's coined practitioner term, cited in the backing block, lines 74/83-84/87), not maintainer-internal repo shorthand — it is what the exercise teaches, displayed as the taught term rather than smuggled maintainer vocabulary.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget — bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Chunk 0 carries 4 bold spans (**Time:**, **What you do:**, **What you build:**, **The point:**) but these are the house exercise-header metadata convention — `grep -l '^\*\*Time:\*\*' curriculum/exercises/*.md` → 37 files use this identical pattern, and the file's own maintainer block (line 56) already attests: "widget chrome (**Time:**, **What you do:**, **What you build:**, **The point:**, **What happened:**) stays bold." Chunk 1's blockquote bold lead (line 19, "Long session, long read.") and chunk 4's (line 42, "The escape hatch is deliberate.") are single callout handles, 1 per chunk, within the ≤1 non-chrome budget. Chunk 5's **What happened:** (line 46) is the same widget-chrome label. Body bullet leads (lines 15-17, 26-27, 31, 35-36) are de-bolded, matching the maintainer note's own claim. No violation.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Presence precedes content — verify against the composed deck, not long-read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: `getting-going.md` line 50 includes this file as a standalone-paragraph include-link (`[Compound and close](exercises/compound-and-close.md)`), the same inclusion mechanism used by every other exercise file in AE101 M1, which reaches the composed deck via `.phase--exercise`. `node scripts/check-slide-size.js --file curriculum/exercises/compound-and-close.md` ran clean and reported "slides: 5" (the file's five `##` sections), confirming the renderer sees the file's sections, not zero.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Numbering — position is computed, content ordinals are linted.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Ran `node scripts/check-slide-numbering.js --file curriculum/exercises/compound-and-close.md` → "OK — 1 files, Phase/Step numbering consistent." File contains no hand-numbered headers or Phase/Step refs at all (headers are plain imperatives), so the check is vacuously satisfied.

rules_evaluated.evidence: Ran `node scripts/check-slide-deixis.js --file curriculum/exercises/compound-and-close.md` → "OK — 1 files, no page-geometry pointers across the slide cut." Manual scan of the body confirms no "below/above/further down/at the top of this page" phrasing.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Slide size — 210 words / 6 bullets, and the cap is machine-checked.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Ran `node scripts/check-slide-size.js --file curriculum/exercises/compound-and-close.md` → "files: 1  slides: 5  limits: 210 words / 6 bullets ... oversized: 0 ... every slide is within limits." No accept-note needed.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Heading grammar is the mood switch, and it is load-bearing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Four of five ## headers are plain exercise imperatives ("Write your rules file...", "Push back where...", "Keep or revert...", "Sweep the session..."), matching the exercise register exactly. The fifth, "What you built" (line 44), is a nominal label, not a declarative claim — it fits the rule's own proposal-time test ("a candidate declaration whose heading is a label rather than a claim is not a declaration yet") and matches an identical house pattern used verbatim or near-verbatim in sibling exercises (`close-the-ticket.md` "## What happened", `author-test-strategy-skill.md`/`map-the-access-surface.md` "## What this sets up") — an established closer-section convention, not a stray declarative.
